annotator: claude-sonnet-5 (opentakeoff-corpus/goals/LINEAR_TAKEOFF.md WP1.7 autonomous coordinator; WP3.8 'ground truth v2' pass added the SAN riser run below)
review_basis: Hand-traced in the running canvas app's Linear tool (manual mode, scale confirmed from the plan's own '1/4" = 1'-0"' note) via a Playwright-driven browser session against the rendered PDF. Before tracing, every text label on this sheet was extracted via pdf.ts's positionedText and cross-referenced against zoomed render crops to locate the pipe-size tick marks ('1 1/4"ø', '1"ø') printed directly on the run, confirming both the run's extent and its size-change point independently of the click coordinates used to trace it. WP3.8 added the SAN riser run: its own dedicated '3" SAN UP' leader was located in a zoomed render crop first, then traced live with the Linear tool's snap engine locking onto the same fitting-cluster vertices the leader points between, and cross-checked against the app's own real-world coordinate readout (both endpoints read x=54'7", confirming a true vertical run) before committing. NOTE added post-WP3.8 (linear-trace-eval.mjs, after walk.ts's dash-gap continuation fix): the CW main golden's own drawn line does NOT dead-end anywhere near its own chosen stop point. Once trace_run could follow the dash-dot line's real print-flattened gaps (previously it dead-ended after 1.63 LF, well short of even discovering this), a seed on this run walks a much longer real trunk -- roughly 35 LF each way before hitting a genuine `ambiguous` junction, passing FIVE real tee branches along the way this golden's own extent doesn't count. This golden's own 3-vertex/18.96 LF extent remains a real, correctly hand-traced representative SPAN of that trunk (still valid for bench/linear.mts's manual-mode parity/totals purposes, and for a human tracing this exact region by hand) -- but it is NOT a fair single-call trace_run comparison target for length/over-trace scoring: the human's own stop point ("the main turns 90° and drops into a riser") is a real, meaningful judgment call, not a hard geometric dead end the walker could independently discover without a human/agent choosing which of several ambiguous branches to continue through, exactly the plan's own §6.3 "offer the candidate fan" design intent. docs/LINEAR-TRACE-EVAL.md documents this as a distinct finding from the dash-gap fix itself.
scope: P101 is dense domestic plumbing (SAN/V/CW/HW branches to every fixture, largely short vertical UP/DN stubs) with no hydronic (HHWS/HHWR) piping anywhere on the sheet. WP1.7 asked for a representative run here, not an exhaustive trace of the sheet; WP3.8's 'ground truth v2' pass adds ONE more representative run rather than closing the gap exhaustively. The CW main golden is ONE domestic cold-water (CW) distribution main: traced from its origin at the 1¼" water-service riser drop (labeled '1¼" CW DN TO WATER SERVICE. COORDINATE WITH FIRE SPRINKLER RISER.') east through an explicit reduction to 1" nominal pipe size, stopping at the point the main turns 90° and drops into a vertical branch riser serving a fixture group. The SAN riser golden added in WP3.8 is exactly the kind of run the original scope deferred: a single vertical UP branch, the 3" sanitary stack running between two fixture-connection clusters near the FD-1/WB-1 fixtures, labeled '3" SAN UP' with its own dedicated leader (distinct from the '2" SAN UP'/'2" SAN DN' labels at each cluster, which describe the fittings themselves, not this straight run). Explicitly still OUT OF SCOPE: the parallel HW (hot water) main on the same sheet, every OTHER SAN and V run (this sheet has dozens of near-identical UP/DN stubs), and the fixture-cluster fittings at each end of the traced SAN riser -- a full branch/fitting-level trace of this sheet is left for a later, broader ground-truth pass.

runs.description: Domestic cold-water (CW) distribution main, from the 1¼" water-service riser junction east to the branch-riser corner near the unit's kitchen/bath fixture group.
3" sanitary (SAN) vertical riser (UP), running between two fixture-connection clusters near the FD-1/WB-1 fixtures.
